title: GS Retail to Launch Second-Half Recruitment for New Employees, Hiring Double Digits per Position - 아시아경제
content:
GS Retail to Launch Second-Half Recruitment for New Employees, Hiring Double Digits per Position GS Retail announced on September 4 that it will launch recruitment for new employees in the second half of 2026. This hiring drive seeks to recruit new employees in double-digit numbers (00 positions) for each business segment, targeting roles in GS25 convenience store sales management, GS The Fresh supermarket store operations, and GS Shop home shopping MD, PD, and marketing positions. Applications can be submitted via the GS Retail recruitment website from September 7 until noon on September 21. The selection process consists of a document screening, AI competency assessment, first-round interview with field professionals, and a second-round executive interview. At GS25 and GS The Fresh, a four-week internship connected to recruitment will be offered after the first-round interview. During the internship period, participants will receive job training and hands-on experience to gain exposure to actual work tasks, thereby enhancing their job understanding and practical capabilities. For GS Shop, new employees will be selected through interviews only, without a separate internship program. Each business segment will focus on strengthening job expertise through hands-on experience. At GS25, employees will have opportunities to build experience in store operations and franchisee communication, allowing them to grow into OFCs (Operations Field Consultants). GS The Fresh provides a pathway to develop store management skills and leadership, ultimately fostering growth into store operations experts. GS Shop supports new employees in building commerce capabilities centered on MD, PD, and marketing positions and in expanding their experience across the entire home shopping business in the future. Jung Youngtae, Head of Human Resources and General Affairs at GS Retail, commented, "Based on our diverse retail businesses such as convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping, GS Retail provides opportunities for new employees to gain a wide range of experience in the field and the company, helping them grow into distribution experts in each area." He added, "We look forward to seeing many applications from candidates who possess 'warmth'—respecting colleagues and growing together—and 'competence'—the ability to proactively achieve results based on professionalism." © The Asia Business Daily. title: GS Retail opens 2026 H2 graduate hiring across convenience, supermarket, home shopping - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: GS Retail(007070) said on the 4th that it will conduct open recruitment for new employees for the second half of 2026 in major business divisions, including convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping. The positions to be hired are GS25 convenience store sales management, GS The Fresh supermarket store sales, and GS Shop MD, PD, and marketing roles. Each business plans to select new employees in double-digit numbers. Applications will be accepted from the 7th to 12 p.m. on the 21st through the GS Retail recruitment website. The process will proceed in the order of document screening, AI competency test, first-round interview with working-level staff, and second-round interview with executives. Applicants for GS25 and GS The Fresh who pass the first interview will undergo a four-week internship linked to hiring. During the internship, they will receive job training, experience actual work in the field, and be assessed for job fit and practical capabilities. GS Shop will select new employees through interviews without an internship. After joining the company, employees will build their careers focusing on the field and roles of each business. New GS25 employees will handle store operations and communication with franchise owners and will be developed into OFCs (sales management experts). At GS The Fresh, they will build store operation and leadership capabilities to grow into store operation experts. Those who join GS Shop will take on MD, PD, and marketing tasks to build the expertise needed for the commerce business. Later, depending on individual capabilities and experience, they can expand their scope of work to various roles within the home shopping business. Chung Young-tae, head of human resources and general affairs at GS Retail, said, "GS Retail provides new employees with opportunities to gain broad experience in the field and the business based on various retail operations such as convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping, and to grow into retail experts in each field," and added, "We look forward to many applications from talented people who possess 'warmth' that respects colleagues and grows together, and 'competence' that proactively delivers results based on professionalism."

title: Vikings Name Captains for 2026 Season - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings on Thursday announced eight season-long team captains for 2026, including three who are assuming the honor for the first time in Minnesota. The following Vikings have been selected via team vote (listed by group in alphabetical order): Offense: Justin Jefferson, Aaron Jones, Sr., Kyler Murray, Brian O'Neill Defense: Blake Cashman, Joshua Metellus, Andrew Van Ginkel Cashman and Van Ginkel were selected by Vikings teammates for the first time as each begins their third season with Minnesota. Murray will serve as a Vikings team captain for the first time; he was a Cardinals team captain every season from 2020-25. A photo of this year's group will be placed in the "Jim Marshall Vikings Captains Legacy" display, which was created in 2024 to honor the 14-time Vikings captain who played every game of the franchise's first two decades. Below is more information on each of the 2026 captains: Cashman shined last season in Purple and racked up a career-high 144 tackles, which are tied for the fifth-most in a single season by a Viking, despite missing four games due to injury. He logged 10 straight games (Week 8-17) with at least nine tackles, becoming the fourth player since 1994 to accomplish the feat. Cashman was the first to do it since Jerod Mayo for the Patriots in 2010. The Vikings signed Cashman in 2024 as a free agent. The Minnesota native was selected by the Jets in the 2019 NFL Draft (157th overall). He played for New York from 2019-21 and for the Texans in 2022 and 2023. Cashman was elevated to captain status in Week 16 of the 2025 season. View photos of Vikings LS Andrew DePaola during the 2025 season. DePaola, a captain for the third consecutive full season, handled all long-snapping duties last season and played in his 150th career regular-season game in Week 15 at Dallas on Sunday Night Football. Following the 2024 season, DePaola earned his third consecutive Pro Bowl nod — becoming the first long snapper in NFL history to do so. He has been selected as an All-Pro (First or Second Team) by The Associated Press in each of the past four seasons. "Jets" started all 17 games in 2025, finishing with 84 catches for 1,048 yards and two touchdowns. In the Vikings finale against Green Bay, he recorded the 37th 100-yard receiving game of his career (eight catches for 101 yards). Jefferson has earned four Associated Press All-Pro nods (First Team in 2022 and 2024; Second Team in 2020 and 2021) and received Pro Bowl honors four times (2020-22, 2024). Through his first six NFL seasons and 94 career games, Jefferson ranks third in catches (579), third in receiving yards (8,480) and seventh in touchdown receptions (42) in Vikings history. He is just nine catches away from passing Randy Moss for second in franchise history. This is Jefferson's fourth consecutive season as a captain. Jones started 12 games for Minnesota in 2025, his first season as a Vikings team captain. He logged 132 carries for 548 yards and two touchdowns, in addition to 28 catches for 199 yards and one touchdown through the air. During the Vikings Week 13 game of 2025, Jones surpassed 10,000 career yards from scrimmage — becoming the 122nd player in NFL history and the fifth active running back/fullback in league history to do so. The Vikings signed Jones in 2024 as a free agent. Originally a fifth-round draft pick by Green Bay in 2017, he spent his first seven NFL seasons for the Packers. He received a Pro Bowl nod following a 2020 campaign in which he had 201 carries for 1,104 yards and nine touchdowns; the previous season, he racked up a career-high 16 TDs. Metellus enters his fifth straight season as a full-time Vikings team captain. He started all 14 games he played in 2025, totaling 86 tackles, one-half sack, two interceptions, a tackle for loss and a career-high six passes defensed. Selected by Minnesota in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft, Metellus started his Vikings career as a special teams stalwart but became a full-time starter in 2023 and has been a Swiss Army knife in Minnesota's defense. In 2023, he was one of five players in the NFL with at least four forced fumbles, 2.0 sacks and an interception. He also was just the third Viking in franchise history to achieve this stat line in a single season, joining Jared Allen (2009 and 2011) and Antoine Winfield, Sr. (2008). Murray enters his first Vikings season after seven in Arizona. The former 2019 No. 1 overall pick started just five games for the Cardinals last season before suffering a foot injury that sent him to Injured Reserve. He was 110-of-161 passing for 962 yards and six touchdowns, while logging 29 carries for 173 yards and a rushing touchdown. Murray started all 87 regular-season games played for the Cardinals. He completed 1,974 of 2,941 pass attempts (67.1%) for 20,460 yards, 121 touchdowns and 60 interceptions with a 92.2 passer rating. He added 532 rushes for 3,193 yards and 32 touchdowns on the ground. O'Neill is entering his ninth NFL season and sixth consecutive as a captain. He has started 120 of 124 regular-season contests and is a two-time Pro Bowler (following 2021 and 2024 seasons). O'Neill grinded through 2025 after suffering an injury during a special teams play in Week 4 in Dublin. View photos of Vikings OLB Andrew Van Ginkel during the 2025 season. Van Ginkel's leadership style is less vocal than some, but he sets an impressive standard by converting hard work and savvy into production. Since joining the Vikings in 2024, Van Ginkel has recorded 133 tackles, 29 tackles for loss, 18.5 sacks, three interceptions, two fumble recoveries, a forced fumble and two defensive touchdowns. title: Karol G in El Paso: Concert times, tickets, parking and entry - El Paso Times
content: El Paso fans are gearing up for the Colombian star Karol G concerts Saturday and Sunday, Sept. 5-6, at the Sun Bowl Stadium. Karol G is bringing her “Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour” to El Paso, with Becky G as a special guest. Becky G appeared as a surprise guest during Karol G's history-making headline set at Coachella in April of this year. Karol G was the first Latina woman to headline Coachella. Before that, they had also shared the stage during Karol G's Mañana Será Bonito Tour in 2023-24. Here is what to know in preparation for Karol G's concerts. The Pay to Park will open at 10 a.m. These parking areas are SB2 along Sun Bowl Drive, SC1, SC2, SC3, and SC4 along Schuster Avenue. HA1 Hawthorne Street and Rim Road, and SC5 on West Schuster Avenue. The Merch Stand will open at 2 p.m. in Glory Field, on Glory Road. Camping is not allowed. Do not arrive earlier than 1 p.m. There will also be merch stands on the second level of the stadium. Selected VIP Packages check-in begins at 4:15 p.m. at the North Gate. Plenty of tickets are still available for Karol G's “Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour." Tickets range from $91 to $446, plus fees, and are available at Ticketmaster.com and the UTEP Box Office. Fans can enter the stadium through any gate (North, South, or East), regardless of the gate listed on their ticket. The West Gate is for ADA and premium ticket holders only. General parking passes will be available for purchase on the day of the event, only at the entrance of each lot. Passes can only be purchased with credit cards. UTEP has contracted with the Goldmine Collective to provide parking services for select University Special Events. ADA parking passes will be available for purchase on a first-come, first-served basis at: Climbing the mountains to watch the concerts is strictly prohibited. Security and law enforcement will be monitoring the perimeter. Noncompliance may result in trespassing violations. The concerts will include lasers, low fog, haze, flames, pyro, and strobing effects. According to the Arizona Republic, Karol G's recent concert at State Farm Stadium in Phoenix was a feast for the eyes as much as it was for the ears. Fireworks, towering flames, dazzling light displays and cascading water effects accompanied different songs, while the massive stage transformed from one act to the next. The main set, built around a towering rocky wall and a pyramid-like structure at its center, constantly evolved through projections, colors and special effects. Use the designated zone at the SB11 Parking Lot at 3333 N. Mesa St. and Kern Drive for pick-up and drop-off. Take the Schuster/Sun Bowl exit (18A) to Sun Bowl Drive. Proceed onto Sun Bowl Drive. Continue towards the roundabout and go straight. At the second roundabout, take a right onto Glory Road. The Sun Bowl Stadium will be on the right. title: Is AI Impacting Global Labor Markets? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. As companies integrate artificial intelligence (AI) tools into their operations, the effects on hiring are starting to show up in the economic data for some industries and workers around the world, according to Goldman Sachs Research. The timing and extent of AI’s impact on job markets depend on the rate of adoption among companies. However, there are inconsistencies in surveys about AI adoption, leading to results that often vary widely. To overcome this, our economists compiled 11 different surveys that measure AI adoption across countries and applied a statistical algorithm to extract rankings, write Goldman Sachs Research economist Sarah Dong and Joseph Briggs, who leads the Global Economics team, in a report. After rescaling around the OECD’s adoption survey­—the most globally comprehensive measure in our economists’ compiled data—Goldman Sachs Research finds that major developed markets are ahead of other countries in deploying AI, with adoption rates between 15%–20%. Among developed markets, France, the US, the Netherlands, and the UK score at the top end of this range of AI adoption. In major emerging markets, adoption rates are in the range of 10%–15%, according to Goldman Sachs Research estimates. Our economists also find that industries with greater exposure to AI automation have been associated with slower growth in job openings since the second half of 2022. The relationship between exposure to AI and slower growth in job openings was more pronounced in Germany, Australia, and the US. “This cross-industry result confirms our prior finding that the onset of generative AI tools may have led companies in highly exposed industries to re-evaluate their hiring plans,” Dong and Briggs write. There is evidence that employment in information and communication services, two of the industries that are the most exposed to AI, has slowed because of AI, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Employment in these sectors has slowed across nearly all major developed markets since 2022. In the US, employment in those industries has fallen below its long-run trend, while it remains near or above the long-run trend in other developed countries. “These patterns suggest tech sector (broadly defined) hiring headwinds are global in nature, although outright negative impacts are most compelling in the US,” Dong and Briggs write. Beyond information and communication services, an assessment of other industries with high exposure to AI reveals a similar, albeit more muted, pattern of AI-related employment headwinds relative to the US. Employment in call centers, software publishing, management consulting, and advertising services has fallen sharply below trend across the developed world. Call center employment, for instance, now stands 39% below trend in the US, 33% below trend in Canada, and 27% below trend in Germany. “These patterns confirm that, like in the US, AI-employment headwinds are visible in industries where labor-automating tools are already available,” Dong and Briggs write. Goldman Sachs Research performed another analysis, which included AI-exposure scores in a cross-country panel for more than 800 occupations, to more rigorously test the impact of AI on employment. Our economists find that a 10% occupational exposure to AI is only associated with a 0.1 percentage point drag to annual headcount growth in France, Canada, and the US. The analysis suggests that “economy-wide hiring headwinds remain limited,” Dong and Briggs write. While AI’s overall impact on job markets appears limited, recent anecdotes and US labor market data suggest that AI displacement could be stronger among entry-level workers. Goldman Sachs Research’s analysis of occupational growth based on entry- and non-entry-level groups signals that junior workers may face greater headwinds to hiring due to AI adoption. “AI-related hiring headwinds are clearly visible in official and unofficial employment data, but impacts are limited to a narrow set of industries and workers,” Dong and Briggs write. title: The National Police Association Endorses the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act - National Police Association
content:
INDIANAPOLIS, September 3, 2026 — The National Police Association (NPA) endorses the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act (H.R. 10070), introduced by Rep. Andy Barr (KY-06) and co-sponsored by Rep. John McGuire (VA-05). This bill expands special overtime pay to U.S. Border Patrol agents at every General Schedule (GS) grade. Under current law, only GS-12 Border Patrol agents receive special overtime pay: an additional 50% of the hourly rate of basic pay for regularly scheduled overtime hours under the Border Patrol Agent Pay Reform Act. That payment is in addition to the 25% overtime supplement lower grades already receive for a scheduled 10-hour workday. The Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act removes the GS-12 restriction, extending the extra 50% overtime payment to agents at all levels. The 25% overtime supplement would remain. It has been referred to the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee; the text for the bill is here. Regardless of service level, Border Patrol agents work long hours in remote and harsh conditions. The dangers and risks they routinely confront, including being targeted by criminal organizations, aren’t limited to a single pay grade. “Border Patrol agents are dedicated public servants committed to the same mission of keeping our borders safe. They should receive consistent overtime pay,” said Paula Fitzsimmons, Legislative Director, National Police Association. Though U.S. Customs and Border Protection has reported increased hiring numbers and a record agent headcount, the agency remains short of its stated force goal of 25,000 agents. Compounding this is an approaching retirement wave that will strain staffing if hiring and retention do not keep pace. “Expanding the special overtime pay benefit to all Border Patrol agents will aid in recruiting, while improving morale and retention among current agents,” Fitzsimmons added. A related Rep. Barr bill called the Border Patrol Supervisors Retention Act (H.R. 8956) introduced earlier this year, would extend the same special overtime to agents at GS-13 through GS-15, who are likewise currently ineligible. The NPA commends Reps. Barr and McGuire for introducing the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act and urges Congress to pass it. content:
Outside linebacker Dallas Turner "ranks among the league's sacks leaders by the end of the season." That's one of the bold predictions that ESPN's Dan Graziano extended this week. Graziano highlighted the third-year Vikings defender who is primed for his biggest role, yet, in his annual all-32 article, in which he selects a potential surprise for each club based on reporting he's done throughout NFL training camps. Graziano says they aren't predictions "in the strictest sense." More so, they are nuggets that "could signal things you might not be expecting." Here's what Graziano is hearing about the 23-year-old Turner, who was the 17th overall pick in 2024: View photos of the Vikings 53-man roster as of Sep. 3, 2026. "In talking to people with the Vikings, it sounds like Turner has reached another gear this offseason and should be positioned to flourish in his third year in Brian Flores' defense. The Vikings need Turner to be a dominant presence off the edge, and during the offseason and training camp, he has impressed teammates and coaches alike with his command of the defense and the advances he has made in technique." To add some color, we will note Turner constantly was in Minnesota's backfield — and Baltimore's backfield during joint practices — this summer, applying pressure and popping through for tackles. When the Ravens were in town, he often matched up against veteran Ronnie Stanley, and he often won. Elsewhere, in the NFC North … here's what Graziano shared in his story: Don't be surprised if … the Bears still trade for an edge rusher. Don't be surprised if … Jameson Williams is the [Lions'] leading receiver. Don't be surprised if …  MarShawn Lloyd takes the [Packers'] starting running back job and — pun intended — runs with it. The latter two offer intrigue because Amon-Ra St. Brown has posted three consecutive seasons of at least 115 catches, 1,250 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. And, Lloyd, a third-round pick by Green Bay in 2024 has only played one NFL game due to multiple lower-body injuries. Recently, new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was touted by The Athletic as one of the 26 most intriguing figures for the 2026 regular season. FOX Sports magnified the focus on Murray even more. Ben Arthur on Tuesday classified "The Kyler Murray Experiment in Minnesota" as the NFL's No. 3 storyline in an article introducing 13 significant ones to monitor. Arthur's explanation is succinct: Released by the Cardinals in the spring after seven seasons, Murray signed a one-year deal at the veteran's minimum with the Vikings and beat out 2024 first-round pick J.J. title: The Adventure Bike With Honda Reliability And Triumph Sophistication - hotcars.com
content: Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update Motorcycles are often fair weather friends. They are great fun on that perfect sunny Sunday morning, but when times get tough that two-wheeled companion can stay locked up in the nice cozy garage. But not adventure bikes. These motorcycles are designed to do everything from blasting across a desert to hacking through a jungle — there is very little that an adventure bike isn't prepared for. We've updated this article with more details on how this bike stacks up against its rivals and a closer look at the different versions available. With a range of accessories, rugged capability, and a comfortable riding position, this is the type of bike that you can rely on when the going gets tough. But there is one that perfectly blends upmarket sophistication with dependable reliability, plus a backstory that begins in one of the world's toughest endurance races. This is one bike you can use on more than just Sunday... Adventure motorcycles, or ADV bikes, are designed to be the Swiss army knives of two-wheeled ownership. These bikes are equally at home on almost any terrain, whether you are traversing the Sahara or riding to Siberia. Of course, a lot of people just use them for regular daily riding, and maybe the odd weekend away, but that's OK. With a comfortable seating position and typically large displacement engines, they soak up the miles on asphalt too. Adventure bikes can trace their history back to scramblers and dirt bikes, with Yamaha bringing the concept to the streets in 1968 with the pioneering DT-1, an off-road machine that could be ridden easily on the streets. By the early '80s, events like the Paris-Dakar race were capturing the public's imagination, and with the rise of backpacking as an alternative to commercial package holidays, bikers realized that motorcycles could take them on adventures they never before dreamed possible. At the forefront of the adventure bike movement was German brand     BMW. While superbikes were all the rage in 1980, BMW decided to buck the trend at the IFMA international show in Cologne. The Bavarian brand unveiled the R80 G/S, a new type of motorbike that was something of a mash-up of every kind of bike you could imagine—the first adventure motorcycle, in fact. It had a capable flat-twin airhead engine, matched to knobby tires, two-up space, and the upright comfort of a tourer. The G/S in the name stood for Gelände/Straße, or "off-road/street" in Teutonic parlance. In 1981, Frenchman Hubert Auriol won the Paris-Dakar Rallye piloting a BMW R 80 G/S, proving the bike's off-road capabilities. Auriol repeated his victory in 1983, while in 1984 and 1985, Belgian Gaston Rahier also won onboard a BMW. In 2018, BMW introduced the new BMW R 1250 GS as the latest in its line of adventure bikes. The Bavarian company has a long history of creating bikes that eat up the miles, and this was designed to be one of the most accomplished. The R 1250 GS features a vastly improved boxer engine with BMW ShiftCam Technology for variation of valve timing and valve stroke on the intake side, with increased power across the entire power band. The 1,254cc powerplant is good for 136 hp at 7,750 rpm and 105 lb-ft of torque at 6,500 rpm. The motor also features asynchronous valve opening on the intake side for improved air-fuel mixture and better effective combustion, along with a knock sensor system to allow for use of variable fuel quality while on the move. The camshaft drive is via toothed chain, replacing a roller chain, and BMW fitted a new exhaust system (with closed-loop catalytic converter technology) for better performance. The oil supply has been improved, and the bike is fitted with the latest generation of BMS-O engine control. As well as taking on the established tech and dependability of the Japanese brands, BMW has also pitched the R 1250 GS against upmarket Triumph. The British brand is known for combining high-tech and sophistication with old-school looks. While the GS doesn't go down the classic styling route, it has plenty of upmarket sophistication that will appeal to the well-heeled Triumph crowd. The GS has connectivity as standard, with a multifunctional instrument cluster that features a large 6.5-inch full-color TFT display. This is supplemented with an analog speedometer and tachometer. These bikes come with two ride modes as standard: ASC (Automatic Stability Control) and Hill Start Control. “Dynamic Traction Control” (DTC), "Dynamic Pro", "Enduro" and "Enduro Pro" ride modes are available as an option. Optional Dynamic ESA means that the bike automatically adapts to riding conditions and movements, as well as providing automatic ride height adjustment. Finally, the BMW Motorrad Spezial has a range of customization features available as factory options. Triumph offers standard factory customization as well as the Triumph Factory Custom (TFC) with ultra-premium options that are often hand-finished. BMW has made its name on a blend of quality and performance, and it seems that the R 1250 GS fits into that. Owners at Advrider.com say there have been some minor issues, but these have reportedly been ironed out, and the bikes have clocked up big mileages. One owner on a Facebook discussion said: "I bought a 2023 R1250 GS Trophy model. Last year of the 1250 GS version. BMW had pretty much completely debugged the model by then. No issues so far." As the bike is so new, it shouldn't cause too many problems, especially if you go for a full service history from an authorized BMW dealership. These bikes are known for clocking up a lot of miles due to the fact they make for good do-it-all machines. As another option, the Honda Africa Twin is seen as the gold standard among the company's adventure bikes. The 2026 model, which employs Honda’s 1,084cc parallel-twin engine, is highly dependable and reliable. The BMW R 1250 GS comes in two flavors, and they target different types of adventure riders. The standard GS is the easier-going option, with a 20-liter tank, adjustable seat, 6.5-inch TFT, boxer engine, shaft drive, and BMW's sophisticated electronic rider aids. For riders who want a more agile machine for daily commuting, tight trails, and weekend touring, the standard bike makes a compelling case. It's lighter at 549 pounds ready to ride, carries a lower seat than the GSA, and is easier to manage at parking-lot speeds. And when things go sideways off-road, there's less motorcycle to wrestle back onto its wheels. Then there's the R 1250 GS Adventure. The GSA adds a huge 30-liter tank, taller suspension, and additional body and engine protection, making it better suited to cross-continent trips, remote terrain, and cold-weather touring. Its taller seat and larger physical footprint also make it a natural choice for tall or larger riders who want extra legroom and a commanding riding position. The BMW R 1250 GS may be the benchmark in big-bore adventure bikes, but there's no shortage of challengers waiting to steal its crown. Triumph comes closest with the Tiger 1200, a direct GS rival that combines a 147-hp inline-three with the same low-maintenance shaft-drive layout. The Triumph has 11 more horsepower than the BMW, but the GS counters with a muscular 105 lb-ft of torque and a more relaxed, low-revving character. For sheer firepower, Ducati and KTM turn the dial way up. The     Multistrada V4 S makes 170 hp, while KTM's 1290 Super Adventure S delivers 160 hp. But peak power isn't the whole story. The BMW's 105 lb-ft of torque actually tops both, beating the Ducati's 92 lb-ft and edging the KTM's 102 lb-ft. The Ducati and KTM also rely on chain final drives that require more routine attention than the BMW's shaft. Honda takes the more dirt-focused route with the Africa Twin Adventure Sports, using its 1,084cc parallel-twin to favor smooth, predictable performance over outright acceleration. Ultimately, each rival has a specialty, but the GS remains the consummate all-rounder, blending strong performance, touring prowess, road manners, off-road capability, sophisticated electronics, and shaft-drive convenience. A 2008 Honda Civic Si will cost on average $15,283, says Classic.com, but for this kind of money you can get a BMW R 1250 GS that is just a few years old. Scouring the classifieds brought up some surprising results. The R 1250 GS cost $22,615 in 2019, but prices are much lower now. On Bringatrailer.com, we found a 2020 bike with 5,000 miles and a BMW-branded top box and side cases that had sold for $15,750. A 2019 bike with 24,000 miles was naturally more affordable, costing just $11,200. The bottom line is that you will need around $15,000, it seems, to get the keys to one of these capable adventure bikes on the used market. As with any used purchase, it's important to do your homework and not be tempted by very low prices, but the R 1250 GS offers a lot of can-do attitude for the money. We want to hear from you. title: Meet U of G’s First Schulich Leaders - U of G News
content: Canada’s largest undergraduate STEM scholarships support entrepreneurial-minded students Learning how to put AI to use for the greater good and helping Canadian farmers with food sustainability are the goals of two Schulich Leaders who will begin their journeys at the University of Guelph this fall. Aryan Thakur will pursue computer engineering and Matteo Volpini will study agriculture with the support of Schulich Leader Scholarships, Canada’s most prestigious STEM scholarship program. Schulich Leader Scholarships provide $100,000 for a science, technology or math degree, or $120,000 for an engineering degree, for entrepreneurial-minded students. U of G is proud to be part of the prestigious scholarship program as it’s a testament to the University’s ability to attract some of Canada’s most competitive STEM students who aspire to careers in tech, engineering and applied research. “As we celebrate 15 years of Schulich Leaders, we are proud to have supported more than 1,000 exceptional Canadian students pursuing STEM degrees at our country’s top universities,” says Judy Schulich, president, The Schulich Foundation. “Schulich Leader Scholarships help attract and retain outstanding talent, empowering the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs. By supporting their ambition and creating the conditions for them to succeed, we can ensure their innovations drive Canada’s future prosperity.” A Schulich Leader Scholarship is life changing, says Aryan Thakur, whose interest in artificial intelligence and machine learning drew him to U of G’s Computer Engineering program in the College of Engineering. As part of a generation who grew up alongside technology, Thakur knew early on he wanted to be part of an industry revolutionizing the world. “AI and machine learning are going to provide a lot of opportunity,” he says, “and I want to align myself with that.” Eager to launch his own start-up, Thakur says his program’s co-op stream is the kind of experiential learning that will build a foundation for him, from which to grow his own ideas. He knows there is work to do in the field. AI is not yet functioning at 100%, and so he is dedicated to being part of improving it, ultimately putting it to use for good. “I want to help people,” he says, “using technology to have a meaningful impact.” Being a Schulich Leader is about more than just financial support, he says. “The ability to network with fellow Scholars really does help with job opportunities or even just aligning with others going through the same life transition.” It was while growing up on a small hobby farm learning tree pruning and how to pick cherries and peaches and apples that Matteo Volpini learned the kind of devastation disease can bring to plants and the crops of farmers. The years his family lost nearly 200 trees to disease, pests and the environment, he started researching where he could study plant science and food sustainability. What he found was the Bachelor of Science in Agriculture program at the Ontario Agricultural College. “I’m excited to learn more about gene-editing technology, gain more plant knowledge and learn how disease affects plants, how pesticides and fungicides can help prevent these things,” he says. His goals don’t end there. “I’d like to start a business dedicated to global food sustainability that supports Canadian farmers by developing resilient crop varieties that can better withstand environmental stressors like pests, disease and unpredictable weather.” As a Schulich Leader, he joins a community of STEM students with similar interests across a broad spectrum of disciplines. “It’s such a great resource to have,” he says. “There are so many opportunities to learn from each other or to collaborate.” Recognizing the increasing importance and impact that STEM disciplines have on the prosperity of future generations, businessman and philanthropist Seymour Schulich established this $200 million scholarship fund in 2012 to encourage our best and brightest students to become Schulich Leader Scholars: the next generation of entrepreneurial-minded, technology innovators. Through The Schulich Foundation and United Jewish Appeal, these prestigious entrance scholarships are awarded to 100 high school graduates enrolling in a science, technology, engineering or mathematics (STEM) undergraduate program at 20 partner universities in Canada. Every high school in Canada can submit one Schulich Leader Nominee per academic year based entrepreneurial leadership and financial need.

title: GS Retail stock slips as fine over data leak and new GS25 dessert shape sentiment - AD HOC NEWS

On September 3, 2026, one domestic market report noted that GS Retail shares finished the session at 25,650 won, down 1.16% from 25,950 won on the prior day, describing the move as a small decline without a specific new negative trigger and pointing to a wait-and-see stance among investors. This mix of modest intraday weakness and a small closing decline suggests that the privacy fine is being absorbed without a sharp repricing, but remains part of the risk assessment for investors looking at the stock’s medium term path. title: This BMW R 1300 GS Comes In A Special Edition With All The Bells And Whistles. But There's A Catch - Yahoo Autos
content: Let's be real: When some motorcycle manufacturers release a special edition, it's only paint and graphics. Now, clearly, we all like things that we find visually appealing, so I'm in no way saying that aesthetics don't matter. However, I'm also the kind of person where, if someone's going to slap a surcharge on something, I want some substance along with my pretties. You know? If you're a Dutch BMW fan, and you have BMW R 1300 GS money in the first place, there's some good news for you. BMW is releasing the Aurum Edition of its R 1300 GS and GS Adventure exclusively in the Netherlands, and although aesthetic touches including a bunch of gold accents (hence the 'aurum,' which is derived from the Latin word for 'gold') and an Alcantara saddle are part of it, the Motorrad also kind of went Huntrix ham on the accessories packages with this one. Can't choose between the Touring package, the Dynamic package, or the Innovation package? Porque no los tres, BMW probably said (only in German)? There will be exactly 100 each of the R 1300 GS and R 1300 GSA Aurum Editions released in the Netherlands, and each will come with its own "XX of 100" numbered badge on the handlebars. The base R 1300 GS that the Aurums are based on, incidentally, is the very popular Triple Black colorway. This Badass Enduro Kit Turns The BMW R1300 GS Into The Rally Bike It Pretends To Be I Thought BMW's R 1300 GS Was Too Tall For Me, But To My Surprise, I Grew To Appreciate It If that's not enough substance to get excited about, then here are the details for each of these special Dutch GS machines. The BMW R 1300 GS Aurum Edition, in addition to getting the factory accessories packages mentioned above, also gets the adaptive ride height and automatic shift assist (ASA), as well as a heated seat, anti-theft alarm, gold spoked wheels, and top case rack. Also, the Option 719 brake and shift levers, a tinted windscreen, and BMW's three-piece Vario luggage come equipped from the factory on this bike. Total cost: € 34,950, which works out to about US $40,601 at the time of writing. If you'd rather go for the BMW R 1300 GS Adventure Aurum Edition, you'll still get all three accessories packages mentioned above. You'll also get the adaptive ride height and ASA features, as well as an anti-theft alarm and top rack. Gold accents, including gold spoked wheels, abound. But you also get blacked out engine protectors (crankcase and valve cover), which are integrated into the blacked-out crash bars. A tinted windscreen and a three-piece aluminum hard luggage set are also included on the GSA only. What's the price? This will set you back a cool € 36,950, which works out to about US $42,925. title: GS Caltex Tightens Defense, Eyes Consecutive Title - 조선일보
content: Defending champions diversify attacks, add Tanacha to reduce Silva's burden after historic win [Cheongpyeong=Sports Chosun Kim Young-rok Reporter] "Through an unexpected championship that no one anticipated, the players have grown significantly. The team has become more solid overall." The 'underdog' achieved a historic championship. Now, they are aiming for a second consecutive title. GS Caltex defied all expectations in the 2025-2026 season, securing third place in the regular season. In the postseason, they achieved six consecutive wins against Heungkuk Life, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, and Korea Expressway Corporation, clinching the championship trophy. This marked the team's first title in six years since the 2020-2021 season. At Cheongpyeong GS Caltex, head coach Lee Young-Taek, discussing preparations for the new season, said, "Although we won the championship, we aimed to bring changes to the team's strength. With Tanacha's addition, we could reduce Silva's burden, and it was impressive to see our players grow even further," expressing pride. "He floated in the air for two days after winning. Now that the new season is approaching, I feel the surrounding expectations. The pressure has definitely increased," he sighed. However, he emphasized, "It became an opportunity to understand how to win championships. The team atmosphere, unity, and focus were excellent. The players themselves know what kind of volleyball they should play, and my task as a coach is to bring that out on the court." Ultimately, GS Caltex's challenge is to reduce reliance on 'queen' Gyselle Silva's attacks. Even after last season's victory, they couldn't avoid criticism like 'ultimately a one-woman Silva championship' and 'Gyselle Silva Caltex.' Silva recorded 1,005 points, 1,008 points, and 1,083 points over three years in Korea, achieving the remarkable feat of scoring over 1,000 points for three consecutive years. However, Silva, born in 1991, is at an age where each year brings significant change. Coach Lee Young-Taek stated, "Scoring over 1,000 points is proof of Silva's consistent outstanding performance, so it's not bad. Still, I want to lessen Silva's attacking burden. This year, we have high expectations for the Asian quota player Tanacha. We aim to demonstrate more diverse attack distribution and ideal volleyball this year." After the championship, the team had a quiet off-season. Compared to the previous season, only the Asian quota player changed from Reina Tokoku to Tanacha Sooksom. Tanacha is in her fourth season in Korea. She is praised for her exceptional stamina and attacking skills and has quickly adapted to GS Caltex. Additionally, the team recruited two Japanese coaches: Kawamura Shinji and Ishii Sugurou. Coach Kawamura has been acquainted with Lee Young-Taek since his playing days and has experience as a coach in the Japanese league. Coach Sugurou is responsible for guiding GS Caltex's young setters: Kim Ji-won, Lee Yoon-shin, and Choi Yoon-young. If Silva and Tanacha are fixed, the remaining wing position is for one outside hitter. Fierce competition is expected among Yoo Seo-yeon, Kwon Min-ji, Lee Ju-a, Kim Ju-hyang, and Kim Mi-yeon. The head coach emphasized, "These are players with strong individuality. There will be timing when bold changes are needed during games. Other players must support Silva well. Now is the time for competition. I hope they show the roles they can play." For middle blockers, Oh Se-yeon has solidified her position, leaving one remaining spot contested between Choi Ga-eun and Choi Yu-rim. title: GS Retail wraps up e-waste recycling campaign with CEO, staff participation - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Retail successfully concluded a used electronics collection event Wednesday morning at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. The event was held as part of the "Our Neighborhood Resource Circulation Campaign," organized ahead of Resource Circulation Day on Sunday in partnership with E-Circulation Governance, a recycling agency under the Ministry of Climate, Environment and Energy. GS Retail CEO Heo Seo-hong, GS25 store owners, and employees from GS Retail and its affiliates brought in their own discarded electronics to take part in the collection drive. Participants received Seoul Milk desserts and coffee from GS25. More than 700 people took part in the event, with over 1,000 used electronic items collected. The items will be processed for resource recycling through E-Circulation Governance. GS Retail plans to expand resource circulation activities for both employees and customers, drawing on its network of more than 18,600 stores nationwide under GS25 and GS The Fresh. Park Gyeong-rang, head of GS Retail's ESG division, said the event was "a meaningful occasion for employees to put the value of resource circulation into practice in their daily lives," adding that the company would "continue to expand a wide range of resource circulation activities going forward."

title: Lunchbreak: Kyler Murray Among The Athletic’s ‘Most Intriguing Figures’ for 2026 - Minnesota Vikings
content:
In a week and a day, the NFL regular season is back. The return begs many questions, one of which The Athletic's Mike Jones recently attempted to answer: Who are some of the most intriguing figures across the league for the 2026 season? Jones took a stab at picking 26 individuals whom "cast longer shadows and own brighter stars." His assessment begins with three quarterbacks: Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes, Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers and Tampa Bay's Baker Mayfield. The first has "already accomplished everything there is to accomplish in this league," said Jones. Except, Mahomes "has never had to deal with serious injury, but now as he enters Year 10, he's working to both complete a full recovery from a torn ACL and put the Chiefs back among the ranks of the NFL's elite." So, there's definitely intrigue. There is too for Rodgers, who proclaimed this as his final season and reunited with former Packers Head Coach Mike McCarthy; and for Mayfield, a gritty player who placed 11th in MVP voting in 2024. View photos of the Vikings 53-man roster as of Sep. 3, 2026. Seven other quarterbacks entered Jones' chat, including new Vikings starter Kyler Murray at No. 15. Jones wrote the following of the two-time Pro Bowl selection: "After [falling short] to live up to potential with the Arizona Cardinals, who took him No. 1 in 2019, Murray receives a fresh start in Minnesota, where he will find himself surrounded by the best supporting cast he has ever worked with in the pros. [Head] Coach Kevin O'Connell has played a role in the career resurrections of both [Sam] Darnold (FYI, No. 13 on Jones' list) and Daniel Jones, and now he'll attempt to do the same with Murray, who beat out J.J. McCarthy midway through training camp. Murray's athleticism should add another dimension to Minnesota's offense, but he'll have to stay healthy — something that proved challenging in Arizona — for the Vikings to contend." For what it's worth, there are two other NFC North entries on Jones' list: Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs (one of two running backs) at 20, plus Bears Head Coach Ben Johnson (one of eight head coaches) at 24. One of them is anticipated to instantly impact the offense. Max Bredeson. At a position that's been somewhat abandoned. Fullback. Andrew Krammer of the Star Tribune on Tuesday detailed how the fifth-round rookie from Michigan is the earliest-selected player at his position (159th overall) since the New York Giants picked former Alabama FB Jalston Fowler with the 108th choice in 2015. Note: Indiana product Riley Nowakowski was listed as a TE by NFL.com in the pre-draft process, but the Steelers are rostering him as a fullback. Nowakowski was drafted 10 slots after Bredeson at 169. In Krammer's article, he points out Bredeson is the next in line in Minnesota's strong fraternity of fullbacks that includes Pro Bowlers Jerome Felton and C.J. Ham; each one thrived before him. View photos of Michigan fullback Max Bredeson who was selected No. 159 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. Krammer shared some of the historical trends of the position that has faded but is not extinct: NFL fullback usage has plummeted from its heyday that extended into the 2000s; 26 fullbacks started at least six games during the 2000 season, per Pro Football Reference. Fullbacks remained prominent into 2012, when Felton was named to the Pro Bowl while blocking for Adrian Peterson's MVP season in Minnesota; that season, 16 teams — or half the league — used a fullback for at least 75 snaps. Over the past decade, only about 10 teams per season have deployed a fullback for at least 75 snaps. title: PIPC narrows GS Retail fine by excluding franchise sales, sparking Korea contrast with Coupang - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Penalty hinges on excluding B2B franchise sales and supermarket revenue after credential-stuffing breach at GS Shop and GS25 In calculating the 12.836 billion won penalty surcharge for a personal data leak imposed on the 31st on GS Retail(24,800 won ▼ 850 -3.31%), the Personal Information Protection Commission excluded franchise supply sales—more than 70% of the company's total revenue—from the benchmark used to compute the surcharge. The move contrasts with the record 624.681 billion won imposed on Coupang three months earlier, confirming that the severity of sanctions can vary widely depending on a retailer's revenue structure. The action stems from an incident in which, from June 2024 to Feb. this year, hackers launched a brute-force login attack on the GS SHOP and GS25 websites operated by GS Retail, leaking the names, contact information, and addresses of 1,661,53 members. According to the industry on the 2nd, the Personal Information Protection Commission viewed about 8 trillion won of GS Retail's roughly 11.5 trillion won average revenue over the past three fiscal years—sales recorded when headquarters supplies goods to franchisees—as unrelated to the violations and excluded it. It judged the revenue to be business-to-business (B2B) transactions with no direct link to the data leak. As a result, the sales figure used as the basis for calculating the penalty surcharge fell to the 2 trillion won range. Under the Personal Information Protection Act, a penalty surcharge is calculated based on total revenue minus revenue unrelated to the violations and cannot exceed 3% of total revenue. The business operator must directly prove the unrelated revenue. GS Retail's business report shows revenue of 11.0803 trillion won in 2023, 11.5794 trillion won in 2024, and 11.9574 trillion won in 2025. The final sticking point was reportedly whether to include sales from the GS The Fresh supermarket chain. GS Retail uses a unified database (DB) across home shopping, convenience stores, and supermarkets, but this attack occurred only at GS SHOP and GS25. Because the DB is shared, some argued supermarket sales should be included, while others countered that a division not actually attacked could not be counted; in the end, supermarket sales were excluded from the benchmark. The attack method also appears to have influenced the outcome. In this incident, hackers used "credential stuffing," repeatedly trying IDs and passwords obtained externally. Because websites with login procedures were targeted, only GS SHOP and GS25 were breached. The commission's internal view was that if the unified DB server itself had been directly attacked, total revenue including supermarkets could have been counted. For that reason, during deliberations, members reportedly raised the view that, going forward, the calculation benchmark could vary depending on the revenue recognition structure, the attack vector, and the scope and types of data leaked. Even if the same company suffers a repeat incident of the same type, there is no guarantee franchise supply sales would be excluded again. The retail industry says the outcome stands in sharp contrast to the Coupang case three months earlier. In June, the Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a total penalty surcharge of 624.681 billion won on Coupang, including 423.575 billion won related to the leak and 201.106 billion won related to infringements such as the unauthorized collection of activity records from other companies' online services. At the time, the Personal Information Protection Commission used the revenue of Coupang's e-commerce service, where the incident occurred, as the benchmark for the surcharge and excluded only divisions separately notified as distinct services, such as Coupang Eats and Coupang Play. During deliberations, Coupang argued that, because it directly purchases goods from manufacturing small and midsize businesses, the entire transaction amount was overstated as its revenue, but the claim was ultimately not accepted. Coupang has said it will file an administrative lawsuit to contest the action. We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze traffic. title: How Karol G’s Sister & Co-Manager Jessica Giraldo Balances the Personal & Professional: ‘I’m Looking Out for Her’ - Billboard
content:
The CEO of Bichota Records is Billboard Español's Executive of the Month. By
												

	Sigal Ratner-Arias Just a few days after kicking off her second global stadium tour, Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, in July, Karol G surprised her fans with the announcement of a new album: No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The 14-track set — which features standout collaborations with Drake and Bruno Mars — was released on Aug. 7 and debuted at No. 1 on Billboard‘s Top Latin Albums chart as well as in the top 10 of the all-genre Billboard 200 (No. 8). It also flooded Hot Latin Songs with 13 entries, led by “Ahí” with Drake, which debuted at No. 1 and was replaced a week later by another hit from the LP, “BbY WOW,” featuring Judeline and Rusowsky. Meanwhile, Karol pledged to donate $1.2 million to relief efforts for communities affected by the Aug. 10 earthquake in Colombia through her Con Cora Foundation. Behind all these achievements is Jessica Giraldo Navarro, CEO of Bichota Records and Karol G’s co-manager and sister. Giraldo Navarro — who leads the label’s global strategy alongside director of label and marketing Luis Mesa — was named Billboard Español‘s Executive of the Month for August. As part of her responsibilities, Giraldo Navarro plays a key role in defining and executing the artist’s career strategy, leading and aligning various teams toward a unified goal; she also supports decision-making and oversees the development and execution of major projects, opportunities and partnerships. Within Bichota Records, she works with Mesa and the wider team to lead and implement the label’s strategy, coordinating various departments and projects to advance Karol’s vision and continue driving the growth of Bichota Records. Billboard Español spoke with Giraldo Navaroo about Karol G’s most recent achievements and initiatives. As CEO of Bichota Records and Karol’s co-manager, how would you sum up this past August? It’s been, literally, a rollercoaster. I’d say that, beyond just August, the last three months have been non-stop work: starting the tour, aligning all the creative elements that are part of the tour — figuring out what works, making adjustments, because the first few shows are about fine-tuning until the tour gets to a point where it runs like clockwork. All of that, in addition to the strategy for the album, which was almost a surprise album that Karol wanted to release that way, without much buildup or pre-launch strategy. As a label and team, we were telling her, “No, we need to start pre-sales three months in advance, we need to release physical albums.” But the way she wanted to release it was very much tied to the album’s concept: like, “I don’t regret feeling so much, and I want to drop this album tomorrow, so I’m dropping it tomorrow.” And it’s been a wonderful surprise: The album is very personal to Karol and has really connected with people. We’re super happy. How have you used the tour to amplify the album release? Obviously, the work has been ongoing: How do we take advantage of the platform we have in all these stadiums, where we’re reaching around 45,000 people every night? How do we use that platform to keep promoting the album? It’s not just about the new segment Karol has created to promote the album, but also about what we can do with the screens, with brand activations. And as we see which songs are connecting with the audience, we go in that direction too. It’s been a great way to measure. You’ve also used the tour to promote the work of the Con Cora Foundation, even before the earthquake in Colombia. Can you tell us about that? Con Cora does an activation at each venue called Mujer Segura (Safe Woman). It’s a space where we provide support and guidance to women on what to do if they feel they’re being harassed or are in danger: which hotlines to call, who to turn to, how to act. It’s a fan activation that connects you to Con Cora on an emotional level. You can leave notes about how you feel, receive guidance, learn about Con Cora and the Mujer Segura program, and find out what to do if something happens during the show — sometimes incidents occur due to alcohol. We make sure they know where to go for help and where our Con Cora staff, who wear identifiable vests, are stationed. In every location, we also take action like visiting a hospital or a shelter for women who’ve been victims of violence, abuse or other trauma. That’s how we’ve integrated our foundation into the tour. But since [the double earthquake of June 24] in Venezuela — which happened near the start of the tour — we’ve been working nonstop. We showed a video about the foundation on the screens, explaining that everything we raised would go to [The House Project], Ricardo Montaner’s foundation. Karol matched all donations we received, including from shows and other donors, and we ended up donating around $400,000 to Venezuela. Then the earthquake in Colombia happened, where the Fundación Con Cora is based. As soon as the tragedy struck, we mobilized our team in Colombia. They went to the most affected areas — we have partner foundations in almost every region of Colombia — to provide on-the-ground support. We delivered essential supplies: food, water, medicine, etc. We know that this stage of the emergency sees a lot of solidarity, but when the news stops being news, the most important phase begins: reconstruction. That’s when many people forget it happened and move on to the next tragedy. So we started with our QR code campaign. At all shows starting in Los Angeles, [where Karol performed at SoFi Stadium on Aug. 14, 15 and 16], we’ve been displaying it on the screens. In L.A., we even used the Infinity Screen to show it throughout the time fans were arriving, during the opening act and after the show, with a message about Con Cora and what we’re doing. Karol also gave a speech during her show, encouraging people to donate, and she pledged to match every donation. We managed to raise $100,000 during the three shows in Los Angeles. Karol was very happy, but she said, “I want to do much more than this. In addition, I, as Carolina Giraldo, will donate $1 million from my own resources.” That’s when we made the decision, and she announced it at the benefit concert Colombia: Voces por la Vida [on Aug. 23]. This is Karol’s second stadium tour, a milestone for a female Latin artist. Did you anticipate going straight into another stadium tour with this album, or was it something you had to work toward? No, you can’t take for granted that you’ll always be able to do a stadium tour. We were even scared to announce it, but fortunately, there were some very big and important things happening in Karol’s career when we decided to launch the tour. Key moments in her career after the first tour and the release of Tropicoqueta solidified her growth, especially with her performance at Coachella [where she became the first Latin woman to headline the festival]. The Victoria’s Secret moment was also huge. But it took going through all of that. It was a process. On this tour, we’re doing 63 shows, plus a few yet to be announced. Right now, 97% of the tour is sold out. Obviously — given how much time is left — we still have Europe and Brazil; Brazil is a harder market to break into, but we’re doing really well there, too. But a global stadium tour with over 90% of tickets sold is something to celebrate. I’d also like to highlight how massive the production has been. Karol always tells me, “I don’t care about the money; I want to outdo myself and give my fans the best experience.” So the investment she’s made in this tour to deliver this production — we have a spectacular show. How do you balance your role as CEO of Bichota Records with being Karol’s co-manager? By having a great team and being able to trust that team. At Bichota Records — with a lot of support from Noah Assad [CEO of Rimas Entertainment and Karol’s co-manager] and Raymond Acosta [of Habibi Management] — we’ve put together a very professional team in marketing, creative and other areas. We also have a very close relationship with [Bichota Records’ distributor] Interscope. Karol is always in close contact with [Interscope Capitol Miami president] Nir Seroussi and Interscope CEO John Janick. So working as a team has made it much easier to handle both the label and a demanding project like Karol’s. And as her sister, I feel like I go the extra mile because, aside from everything else, I’m looking out for her. What has been Interscope’s role beyond the distribution agreement? In our agreement with Interscope, there’s a really cool bonus: they provide their entire machinery and teams in Miami, Los Angeles and internationally to work with us. So we come up with a strategy at the office, present it, and they go all in. It’s 100% a team effort. And with this album release, which includes two major international collaborations with Bruno Mars and Drake, I can tell you that Interscope has been leading a big part of the work we’ve been doing. Where do you see Bichota Records in five years? Do you think you’ll sign other artists? A lot of emerging artists reach out to us for help. They’ll call and say, “I want to record, I want to sign with a publisher.” So I connect them with the right people. Or they’ll say, “I need advice on this,” and I connect them with the right contacts. It’s been a very collaborative space for emerging artists and even for other industry artists who might need something from us. But for now, signing other artists isn’t in our plans; we’re 100% focused on Karol G as far as the label is concerned. What’s the biggest challenge and greatest satisfaction of working with your sister? It’s a challenge, but also extremely gratifying. Karol and I, beyond just being sisters, are best friends: when something happens to her, I’m the first person she calls, and vice versa. So sometimes I worry that, at some point, a disagreement or conflict could affect the relationship we have. But we’ve “managed” — in quotes, because sometimes it’s almost impossible — to separate the professional from the personal. I never take anything personally; neither does she. It’s also incredibly satisfying to see that everything we’ve accomplished has been very family-oriented. My dad was also involved in the project for many years. He’s no longer as involved, but we’re a very close-knit family, so we celebrate all the achievements together. Seeing that it’s still something very family-driven is extremely rewarding. content: Investment banking (IB) activity at The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS gathered significant momentum in the first half of 2026, aided by improving dealmaking and capital market conditions. The company’s IB fees jumped 52% year over year to $6.24 billion, driven by broad-based strength across advisory and underwriting businesses in the first half of 2026. The improvement was particularly pronounced in equity underwriting. In the first six months of 2026, advisory revenues increased 46% year over year to $2.87 billion, while equity underwriting revenues surged 90% to $1.52 billion. Debt underwriting revenues advanced 37% to $1.84 billion. In the second quarter alone, IB fees climbed 55% to $3.40 billion. Equity underwriting benefited from higher secondary and initial public offerings, while debt underwriting was supported by increased leveraged-finance and asset-backed activity. Advisory revenues gained from higher industry-wide completed M&A volumes. Goldman’s strong competitive position has further supported the momentum. In the second quarter, the company remained #1 in announced and completed M&A, equity and equity-related offerings, and leveraged lending, while ranking #2 in high-yield debt. This leadership underscores the strength of its global franchise and its ability to capture opportunities as corporate transaction activity improves. Further momentum in Goldman’s investment banking business will likely be supported by robust strategic M&A activity, AI-related capital formation, stronger financing demand, and improving equity and debt underwriting activity. The firm’s investment banking backlog has reached a five-year high, including a record advisory backlog, providing good revenue visibility. Its leading positions in announced and completed M&A, equity and equity-related offerings, and leveraged lending should also help it capture a greater share of improving capital-market activity. Nonetheless, the pace of recovery could remain uneven. Deal completions and IPO activity are sensitive to market volatility, economic conditions, financing availability, trade-policy uncertainty, geopolitical developments and regulatory approvals. Overall, Goldman’s strong market position, improving capital market backdrop and elevated backlog suggest that IB momentum is likely to remain healthy, though the magnitude of growth will depend on how quickly the robust pipeline translates into completed transactions. Similar to GS, its close peers, JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS, are benefiting from industry-wide improvement in the operating environment. JPMorgan remains well-positioned to benefit as capital markets and advisory activity normalize over time. In the first half of 2026, JPMorgan captured a 9.3% wallet share. Looking ahead, a healthy pipeline and resilient M&A demand (as companies seek scale, cost synergies and enhanced technology capabilities to remain competitive) are expected to support the IB business. Morgan Stanley's IB franchise continues to recover as issuance and strategic activity improve. In the first half of 2026, IB fees jumped 47% year over year. title: 2027 BMW F 450 GS: First Look - Top Speed
content: With a Master's degree in English Literature and six years of writing experience, Aayush has been contributing to TopSpeed for over two years. Since 95% of his personality is motorcycles, he goes beyond the spec sheet to explore the culture and spirit of motorcycling. Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Lightweight adventure bikes are all the rage these days, and BMW is making a more serious push with its newest ADV offering: the 2027 BMW F 450 GS. Unveiled as a production model at EICMA 2025, the F 450 GS is a dynamic all-rounder sub-500cc adventure bike expected to reach BMW dealerships in the US late this year or early next year. While BMW hasn’t revealed the North American MSRP yet, here’s how this new adventure bike fills a gap in the sub-500cc class. The sub-500cc ADV segment has a gap: a lack of a premium all-rounder. That’s exactly what the BMW F 450 GS is positioned as. According to Markus Flasch, CEO of BMW Motorrad, the F 450 GS is a genuine GS in the A2 class, where most sub-500 cc ADVs fall. The new GS is powered by a 48-horsepower parallel-twin, bringing proven GS technology and iconic design. BMW says the new GS strikes a balance between agility and stability and should be impressive both on and off the road, serving as a versatile all-rounder for riders seeking a dynamic, premium riding experience. Compared to the older G 310 GS, the new GS is much more modern, packed with cutting-edge features, and delivers as much performance as A2 homologation allows. For the US, BMW will only offer the top-tier GS Trophy variant. BMW says the F 450 GS combines classic GS spirit with modern accessible performance, and that’s largely down to its newly developed powerplant: a 420cc parallel-twin engine. The engine is rated at 48 horsepower at 8,750 RPM and 32 pound-feet of torque at 4,750 RPM. In addition, it uses a unique 135-degree crankpin and a single balance shaft, which are said to offer plenty of character without compromising smoothness. BMW cites an incredibly economical 60 mpg, resulting in a 217-mile theoretical fuel range out of the 3.6-gallon fuel tank. The parallel-twin is mated to a 6-speed transmission with Shift Assist Pro, but what makes the F 450 GS unique in the segment is the BMW Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), standard on the GS Trophy variant. It’s a further development of a centrifugal clutch, completely eliminating the need to manually operate the clutch lever while riding. The bike still retains a traditional clutch lever, letting you take control when required. In this sub-500cc space, no other motorcycle offers this. The F 450 GS uses a newly developed lattice-tube frame that employs the engine as a stressed member, and BMW says its short wheelbase should offer agile, playful handling. Suspension duties are handled by a 43mm KYB inverted fork, adjustable for rebound and compression damping on up-spec Sport and GS Trophy models. In the rear, a non-link-type KYB monoshock featuring spring-preload and rebound damping adjustment regardless of trim. The suspension setup offers 7.1 inches of wheel travel at either end, which is fairly competitive within the category. The GS Trophy edition also brings 19/17-inch tubeless cross-spoke wheels. And braking comes from a Brembo 4-pot caliper working on a 310mm floating disc up front and a 1-pot floating caliper gripping a 240mm rear disc. Combined, the underpinnings setup is said to give the bike a balanced power-to-torque ratio, and the bike tips the scales at 390 pounds ready to ride. The BMW F 450 GS is also designed to suit a variety of motorcyclists, with 3 seat options: a 33.3-inch flat seat as standard, plus a low seat (32.7-inch) and a high Rallye seat (34-inch). The tapered aluminum handlebar can be raised by 20mm with the available riders, while the hand and foot levers are adjustable. The GS Trophy edition also features wider enduro pegs as standard, with removable rubber grips for better off-road grip. Finally, wind protection is handled by a short Rallye windscreen, with a taller one on offer. The F 450 GS is designed along the lines of its larger siblings, and it also brings some of the GS-proven tech, including the iconic X daytime running lights and a 6.5-inch TFT display. Four riding modes, including Rain, Road, Enduro, and Enduro Pro, let you dial in the riding experience. And rider aids include ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control, Dynamic Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR). BMW also offers plenty of optional extras, including an Akrapovič muffler, protection parts, and luggage options. According to Astrid Neudecker, Product Manager, BMW F 450 GS, the new Beemer ADV is designed for a wide range of motorcyclists looking for lightweight versatility and riding pleasure without compromising on cutting-edge technology. And that’s what makes the F 450 GS unique in the segment. It’s positioned as a 50-50 adventure bike that balances both on- and off-road abilities, so, in theory, it can handle whatever you throw at it. Its primary rivals include the parallel-twin adventure tourers from Japan, like the Kawasaki KLE 500 and the Honda NX 500. Both are more on-road focused due to their chassis and engine character, while also lacking similar premium-level electronic features. Meanwhile, the KTM 390 Adventure R and Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 are capable off-roaders but their single-cylinder powerplants won't deliver the same kind of smoothness associated with parallel-twin engines. The CFMoto Ibex 450 is the most competent rival when comparing specification sheets and will be more affordable. BMW offers four variants of the F 450 GS in other markets, but the United States will only get the top-spec F 450 GS Trophy edition, at least initially. No pricing information has been made available for North American markets yet, though UK and European pricing suggests it will be on the pricier end of the spectrum when it arrives. This variant brings the iconic Racing Blue Metallic Paint, wider off-road footpegs, hand guards, engine guard, Gear Shift Assist Pro, Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), sports suspension, and cross-spoke wheels. Expect the F 450 GS to arrive at your nearest BMW dealer later this year or earlier in 2027. Look to this space for more updates on the F 450 GS.
